keysecondary: Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry
1.content:
Hogwarts is a Scottish wizarding school located in the Scottish Highlands. It accepted any magical student residing in the islands of Great Britain and Ireland at the age of eleven years old at the start of the incoming term for enrolment. It's a state-owned school, funded by the British Ministry of Magic.

Hogwarts students are divided into four houses: Gryffindor, Hufflepuff, Ravenclaw, Slytherin.
secondary_keys: Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry
1.name: Hogwarts

2.content:
Gryffindor is one of the four Houses of Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry and was founded by Godric Gryffindor. Gryffindor instructed the Sorting Hat to choose students possessing characteristics he most valued, such as courage, chivalry, nerve and determination, to be sorted into his house.

House symbol: Lion
House colours: Deep red and gold
House ghost: Nearly Headless Nick
Common room: The entrance to the common room was on the seventh floor hidden behind a portrait of the Fat Lady. To enter, the correct password must be provided.
Gryffindor students: Harry Potter, Ron Weasley, Hermione Granger, Fred Weasley, George Weasley, Ginny Weasley, Neville Longbottom, Lavender Brown, Parvati Patil, Seamus Finnigan, Dean Thomas, Lee Jordan, Percy Weasley, Oliver Wood, Colin Creevey.
2.name: Gryffindor

3.content:
Hufflepuff is one of the four Houses of Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry. Its founder was the medieval witch Helga Hufflepuff. Hufflepuff is the most inclusive among the four houses, valuing hard work, dedication, patience, loyalty, and fair play rather than a particular aptitude in its members.

House symbol: Badger
House colours: Yellow and black
House ghost: Fat Friar
Common room: Located near the kitchens. To enter, one must tap a fake barrel in the rhythm "Helga Hufflepuff." It was the only common room to have a way to keep students from other houses out (by dumping vinegar on them).

Hufflepuff students: Nymphadora Tonks, Pomona Sprout, Newton Scamander, Theseus Scamander, Cedric Diggory, Hannah Abbott.
3.name: Hufflepuff

4.content:
Ravenclaw is one of the four Houses of Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry. Its founder was the medieval witch Rowena Ravenclaw. Members of this house are characterised by their wit, learning, and wisdom. The emblematic animal symbol is an eagle, and blue and bronze are its colours. The Head of Ravenclaw is Filius Flitwick, and the House ghost is the Grey Lady, real name Helena Ravenclaw, daughter of Rowena.

House symbol: Eagle
House colours: Blue and bronze
House ghost: The Grey Lady
Common room: Located in a high tower, and the interior was decorated with blue and bronze. To enter, one must answer a riddle from an eagle door knocker.
Ravenclaw students: Luna Lovegood, Cho Chang, Padma Patil.
4.name: Ravenclaw

5.content:
Slytherin is one of the four Houses at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry, founded by Salazar Slytherin. In establishing the house, Salazar instructed the Sorting Hat to pick students who had a few particular characteristics he most valued. Those characteristics included cunning, resourcefulness, leadership, and ambition.

House symbol: Serpent
House colours: Green and silver
House ghost: The Bloody Baron
Common room: Located in the dungeons, underneath the Black Lake, and hidden behind a stone wall. To enter, the correct password must be provided.

Slytherin students: Draco Malfoy, Vincent Crabbe, Gregory Goyle, Pansy Parkinson, Theodore Nott, Oliver Grindelwald, Marcus Flint, Blaise Zabini.
5.name: Slytherin

6.content: A spell that summons an object towards the caster. It is able to summon objects in direct line of sight of the caster, as well as things out of view, by calling the object aloud after the incantation (unless the spell is casted nonverbally). This spell needs thought behind it, and the object must be clear in the casters mind before trying to summon it. The caster doesn't necessarily need to know the location of the target if they say the name of the object to be summoned.
6.name: Accio

7.content: A conjuration that produces a clean, drinkable jet of water from the wand tip.
7.name: Aguamenti

8.content: A spell that unlocks doors and other locked objects. It can also unlock doors that have been sealed with a Locking Spell, although it is possible to bewitch doors to become unaffected by this spell.
8.name: Alohomora

9.content: A spell that reveals secret messages written in invisible ink, or any other hidden markings. Also works against Concealing charms.
9.name: Aparecium

10.content: A spell that reveals traces of magic, including footprints and track marks.
10.name: Appare Vestigium

11.content: A transportation that magically transports the caster to another location instantaneously. The destination is one that the primary user has been to or seen in some fashion previously. Can be used to apparate multiple people at once if holding each other. No incantation required.
11.name: Apparition

12.content: A spell that decreases the velocity of a moving target. Can be used on multiple targets, as well as on the caster themselves.
12.name: Arresto Momentum

13.content: A spell that lifts the caster high into the air. The charm also works underwater, propelling the caster above the surface.
13.name: Ascendio

14.content: A curse that causes instantaneous death. It is accompanied by a flash of green light and a rushing noise. There is no known Counter-curse that can protect the victim from dying, except for a loving sacrifice. It is one of the three Unforgivable Curses.
14.name: Avada Kedavra

15.content: A spell that provokes a small explosion.
15.name: Bombarda

16.content: A spell that locks doors and all things that can be locked. It is the counter-charm to the Unlocking Spell.
16.name: Colloportus

17.content: A spell that causes the victim to become confused and befuddled.
17.name: Confundo

18.content: A curse that inflicts intense pain on the recipient of the curse. This curse does not physically harm the victim, but may in extreme cases drive them insane. The pain is described as having hot knives being driven into the victim. It cannot be cast successfully by a person who is doing so out of pure spite or anger; one must feel a true desire to cause the victim pain. If one casts this spell, he or she will receive a life sentence in Azkaban prison for it, as with the other two Unforgivable Curses.
18.name: Crucio

19.content: A counter-charm to the Reverse Spell, vanishing the image of the last spell cast. It may also disintegrate other certain images.
19.name: Deletrius

20.content: A spell that sends the target away from the caster. It is the counter-charm to the Summoning Charm.
20.name: Depulso

21.content: A spell that causes object to fall or move downwards.
21.name: Descendo

22.content: A spell that used to precisely cut or tear objects.
22.name: Diffindo

23.content: A spell that forces the target to shrink.
23.name: Diminuendo

24.content: A spell that used to open passages.
24.name: Dissendium

25.content: A spell that causes the target to swell in physical size. Its counter-charm is the Shrinking Charm.
25.name: Engorgio

26.content: A healing spell used to heal relatively minor injuries, such as broken bones and cartilage.
26.name: Episkey

27.content: A spell that used to erect a tent or other upright structure.
27.name: Erecto

28.content: A spell that throws the victim backward, similarly to being thrown.
28.name: Everte Statum

29.content: This charm is a highly powerful and advanced protective spell which will conjure a spirit guardian of their positive emotions to defend against dark creatures; it can also send messages to other witches or wizards. The Patronus takes the form of an animal, unique to each person who casts it. The form of a Patronus can change when one has undergone a period of heightened emotion.
29.name: Expecto Patronum

30.content: A spell that forces whatever an opponent is holding to fly out of their hand.
30.name: Expelliarmus

31.content: A curse that provokes an explosion, unique in that it uses pressure to do so as opposed to heat.
31.name: Expulso

33.content: A counter-spell that terminates all spell effects in the vicinity of the caster.
33.name: Finite Incantatem

34.content: A spell that writes in midair with firey marks.
34.name: Flagrate

35.content: A jinx that knocks objects and creatures backwards.
35.name: Flipendo

36.content: A spell that duplicates the target. When used to duplicate objects indefinitely on purpose, is known as the Gemino Curse.
36.name: Geminio

37.content: A spell that freezes the target with icy-cold air.
37.name: Glacius

38.content: A spell that reveals human presence in the vicinity of the caster.
38.name: Homenum Revelio

39.content: A spell that makes writing impossible to read.
39.name: Illegibilus

40.content: A spell that immobilises and stops the actions of the target. It works both on living and inanimate things.
40.name: Immobulus

41.content: A jinx that slows down or stops the target.
41.name: Impedimenta

42.content: A curse that places the victim completely under the caster's control. The victim is put into a trance-like state, and becomes very suggestible to the commands of the caster. However, those who are strong willed may learn to resist it. One of the three "Unforgivable Curses," the use of this curse on another human results in capital punishment or life sentence in Azkaban.
42.name: Imperio

43.content: A conjuration that ties up the target with ropes conjured from thin air.
43.name: Incarcerous

45.content: A jinx that inflates the target, filling it with air.
45.name: Inflatus

46.content: A spell that allows the caster to delve into the mind of the victim, allowing the caster to see the memories, thoughts, and emotions of the victim.
46.name: Legilimens

47.content: A jinx that hoists people up into the air by their ankle.[56] Created by Severus Snape.
47.name: Levicorpus

48.content: A jinx that the counter-jinx to Levicorpus.
48.name: Liberacorpus

49.content: A spell that illuminates the tip of the caster's wand, allowing the caster to see in the dark.
49.name: Lumos

50.content: A spell that produces a blinding flash of bright white light from the tip of the wand. It is a variant of the Wand-Lighting Charm.
50.name: Lumos Maxima

51.content: A spell that levitates and moves bodies.
51.name: Mobilicorpus

52.content: A dark charm that conjures the Dark Mark, which is the sign of the Death Eaters.
52.name: Morsmordre

53.content: A spell that prevents others from hearing nearby conversations by filling peoples' ears with an unidentifiable buzzing.
53.name: Muffliato

54.content: A spell that extinguishes wandlight. It the counter-charm for the Wand-Lighting Charm, Lumos.
54.name: Nox

55.content: A spell that creates fog from the tip of the wand.
55.name: Nebulus

56.content: A spell that erases specific memories.
56.name: Obliviate

57.content: A conjuration that blindfolds the target.
57.name: Obscuro

58.content: A curse that used to temporarily bind the victim's body in a position much like that of a soldier at attention; the victim will usually fall to the ground.
58.name: Petrificus Totalus

59.content: A spell that forces a wand to show an "echo" of the last spell it performed.
59.name: Prior Incantato

60.content: A invisible shield that reflects spells and blocks physical entities.
60.name: Protego

61.content: A dark charm conjures a protective ring of black fire around the caster that only affects their enemies.
61.name: Protego Diabolica

62.content: A spell that protects an area for an extended period of time.
62.name: Protego totalum

63.content: A curse that breaks objects. In stronger usages, disintegrates them.
63.name: Reducto

64.content: A spell that seamlessly repairs broken objects.
64.name: Reparo

65.content: A spell that reveals secrets about a person or object.
65.name: Revelio

66.content: A curse that Lacerates the target, as if they have been "slashed by a sword." Subsequently, the target can easily bleed to death from the wounds. This curse was invented by Severus Snape, to be used against his personal enemies.
66.name: Sectumsempra

67.content: A spell that stuns the target, rendering them unconscious.
67.name: Stupefy

68.content: A healing spell that slows blood flow, clears residue, and knits wounds. It is the counter-curse to Sectumsempra.
68.name: Vulnera Sanentur

69.content: A spell that makes objects fly, or levitate.
69.name: Wingardium Leviosa

70.content:
Tom Marvolo Riddle, later known as Lord Voldemort or, alternatively as the Dark Lord, You-Know-Who, or He-Who-Must-Not-Be-Named is an English half-blood wizard considered to be the most powerful and dangerous Dark wizard of all time. He is amongst the greatest wizards to have ever lived, rivalled only by Albus Dumbledore. Descended from Salazar Slytherin on his mother's side through the House of Gaunt.

Tom began attending Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry in 1938 and was immediately sorted into Slytherin house. During this time, Tom discovered his heritage and adopted pure-blood supremacist ideals. Tom opened the Chamber of Secrets and used its monster, the Basilisk, to attack Muggle-born students, resulting in the death of Myrtle Warren. He began his quest to attain immortality between the years of 1943 and 1998, creating his first Horcrux at the age of sixteen. While attending Hogwarts, Tom Riddle was made a prefect in 1942 until his graduation in 1945.
70.name: Voldemort

71.content:
Nagini is a Maledictus cursed to transform into a snake. Originating possibly in Indonesia, by 1927 she was a performer at the Circus Arcanus where she met Credence Barebone and had a romantic relationship with him. By then, she could transform into a snake at will, although her curse did often cause her to transform uncontrollably.

By 1994, Nagini was seemingly trapped in snake form and belonged to Lord Voldemort, with whom she had a special bond largely due to becoming a Horcrux after her master had killed Bertha Jorkins that same year.
71.name: Nagini

72.content: The Death Eaters were the most ardent followers of Lord Voldemort. The group primarily consisted of wizards and witches who were radical pure-blood supremacists who practised the Dark Arts with reckless abandon, malevolence and without regard to or fear of wizarding law, although some of them joined him out of fear or were blackmailed to do so.
72.name: Death Eaters

73.content:
Hogsmeade, is the only all-wizarding village in Britain. It was founded by Hengist of Woodcroft. Since before 1714 (when the 1714 Edict was passed), Hogwarts third-years and above had been permitted weekend trips into the village.

Mainly, students frequented the High Street in the village, which contained the named speciality shops and pubs such as Zonko's Joke Shop and Honeydukes. Otherwise, they wandered on to observe the infamous Shrieking Shack.

Hogsmeade is a picturesque little village of cottages and shops, with enchanted candles hanging in the trees during the holidays. It is also near the location of the train station used by the Hogwarts Express.
73.name: Hogsmeade

74.content:
Diagon Alley is a cobblestoned wizarding alley and shopping area located in London, England behind a pub called the Leaky Cauldron. Inside the alley is an assortment of restaurants, shops, and other sights. All items on the Hogwarts supply list could be bought at Diagon Alley.

The alley is completely hidden from the Muggle world, which is right outside of its boundaries. It is very large in area and essentially the centre of wizarding London.
74.name: Diagon Alley
